messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: High fncall/structured-output surge detected on api-hosts-us-east. Recommend immediate tenant-scoped mitigations: restrict tool/function calling and switch to text-only fallback for impacted tenants. Incident INC-20260317-01.

maya: taking pager. looking at dashboards now — spike concentrated to tenant acme-prod.

aj: confirming. toolproxy error rate ~12%, p99 latency up ~300ms. affected: acme-prod, beta-saas.

siva: recommended quick plan: 1) apply tenant rate limits for toolcalls 2) disable structured output (fncall/json) for impacted tenants 3) notify customers + enable 429s for throttle signaling. runbook: https://redwood/runbooks/toolcall-surge

ops-bot: running command: /tenant-action acme-prod set_rate_limit --calls-per-min 20 --reason "auto-mitigate surge"

ops-bot: DONE: rate cap applied to acme-prod -> 20/min (opcode 0x9f3).

nina: maya, can we flip structured-output off for acme-prod now? that'll reduce executor load quickly.

maya: doing /feature-toggle structured_output --tenant=acme-prod --state=off

maya: DONE. structured-output disabled for acme-prod. fallback = text-only. audit id fd3a1b.

aj: note: integrations that rely on fncalls will start degrading. CS alerted.

leo: quick question — any chance to raise cap for critical tenants instead of blanket disable? might keep some automations live.

siva: raising caps increases exec surface. prefer rate-limit + text-only first. we can enable canary passes for select nodes.

maya: creating canary rule: allow toolcalls on 2 nodes only (canary-24) to validate critical flows without full load.

ops-bot: CANARY: canary-24 applied -> nodes: node-11,node-12.

aj: metrics: within 90s after actions p99 dropped from ~420ms to ~160ms, toolproxy 5xxs falling.

ops-bot: incident note appended: applied tenant-scoped toolcall ratecaps, disabled structured-output for acme-prod and beta-saas, deployed canary nodes. Ticket INC-20260317-01 updated.

nina: let's also make the proxy return 429 + Retry-After for rate-limit responses so clients can backoff gracefully instead of getting 5xx. fast patch?

siva: simple edge rewrite: rewrite_response(429, {"Retry-After":"30"}) in proxy policy. I can push.

maya: pushed proxy rule as hotfix PR#4851 -> rolled within 30s. test harness shows 429s with Retry-After heading.

customer-success: CS update drafted and sent to acme CSM and beta-saas leads: "We applied protective throttles and switched to text-only outputs to stabilize latency. No data loss expected. We'll follow up at 30m and 1h with status."

leo: customers reporting lower error rates but some automation jobs lost fncalls — CS to coordinate re-runs.

aj: handoff: maya is primary for the next 45m while I prepare postmortem skeleton. escalate to eng-sre if not recovered within 10m.

maya: checklist copied to incident: - collect prompt traces for acme-prod - save sample requests that triggered toolcalls - attach logs fd3a1b & canary traces - schedule postmortem.

ops-bot: Timeline entry: 4105002468 apply ratecap -> 4105002475 disable structured-output -> 4105002490 canary deploy -> 4105002505 proxy 429 patch.

aj: monitoring looks stable. closing pager -> status: mitigated, but keep alerting on for 1h.

incident-bot: Incident INC-20260317-01 status changed to MITIGATED. Actions recorded and owners assigned. Follow-ups: postmortem + customer exec summary. Link: https://redwood/incidents/INC-20260317-01

maya: I'll own postmortem write-up and customer follow-ups. will post summary in #incidents within 24h.

customer-success: acked. continuing direct comms with customers.

maya: closing thread for now. re-open if we see regression. thanks all :thumbsup:
